titulo_es: What I would have done: conditional passato

avrei dovuto.en: It should have; it should have been

avrei voluto.consejo: Unfulfilled desire expression in the past.

ringraziare.consejo: Regular verb of the first conjugation.

texto: **avere** or **essere** + participle conditional: **avrei mangiato** (had eaten), **sarei andato** (had gone). The auxiliary usually follows the one with the main verb in the composite times: **sarei partito**, **avrei telefonato**.
With **dovere, potere, volere** the variation is preserved: **avrei dovuto partire** and **sarei dovuto partire** are possible; it serves the infinitive auxiliary.

bloques.titulo: Avrei dovuto, avrei potuto, avrei voluto
texto: With modal verbs: **avrei dovuto** (would have due), **avrei potuto** (would have been able), **avrei voluto** (would have wanted).

filas: I would have wanted to come.

bloques.titulo: Ieri ti ho invite alla festa

frases.it: Ieri ti ho invitato alla festa.
frases.es: Ayer te invité a la fiesta.
frases.en: I invited you to the party yesterday.
What a shame! You should have come.
You're right. I would have wanted to come.
analisis: I would have wanted to come.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «I would have gone.» in Italian (a man)?

opciones.explicacion: «Andare» rules the «essere» Auxiliary and is agreed on masculine singular.
«Andare» never selects the «avere» Auxiliary.
It's a simple present conditional: «I'd be right there.».

bloques.frase: Avrei ___ venire con voi alla conferenza.

opciones.explicacion: Regular seminary of the modal verb «volere».
He is the third plural person in the present: «They want to».
It is the simple form of this conditional: «querría».

bloques.pregunta: What is the expression of this reflection?
bloques.frase: Avrei dovuto studiare di più per l'esame.

opciones.texto: I should have studied more for the test.
opciones.explicacion: Dissenting of a past obligation not fulfilled.

opciones.texto: I have to study for the test right now.
opciones.explicacion: This obligation is at present.

opciones.texto: I studied a lot for the test yesterday.
opciones.explicacion: It contrasts the meaning of untapped opportunity.

bloques.pregunta: What does the speaker communicate in this sentence?
bloques.frase: Ti ho invitato alla festa di sabato.

opciones.texto: I invited you to the party on Saturday.
opciones.explicacion: Passato prossimo communicating the invitation given.

opciones.texto: I'll invite you to a party next month.
opciones.explicacion: It would be projected in the future with «ti inviterò».

opciones.texto: I don't want to invite you to any party.
opciones.explicacion: Denial opposed to the content of the prayer.

bloques.frase: Non sono venuto alla festa perché lavoravo
bloques.traduccion: I didn't come to the party because I was working.
bloques.explicacion: Justification in the past with prossimo and imperfect prossimo.

bloques.pregunta: I would have been able to (io)
bloques.frase: Con più tempo libero, io ___ potuto aiutarti volentieri.

opciones.explicacion: «avere» conditional to form the passato condizionale with «potuto».
«Sono potuto» does not form the composite conditional but the prossimo passage.
«Avevo potuto» is prossimo trapassate, not conditional.

bloques.pregunta: What does the «purtroppo» warning mean in an answer?

opciones.explicacion: It expresses regret or regret at an unfavourable fact.
It would be «per fortuna».
It would respond to the «comunque» warning.

bloques.pregunta: What is the right way for «You should have come.» (you)?

opciones.explicacion: Condition composed of the second person singular of «avere».
It is an incorrect construction that omits the modal partition «dovuto».
It corresponds to the prossimo-indicative trapassate.

intro: Sometimes you talk about something that didn't happen: what you would have done, or what you should have done. That's the last parole.
